mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, which reduces consumer savings and increases wage pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when UNRATE < 5.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of YoY GDPC1 decline exceeding -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based demand contraction, which increases recession probability and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a six-month window signals a data inconsistency or measurement artifact rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically coincides with subsequent negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to market skepticism.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when the six-month correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE exceeds 0.5.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in inflation, which prompts aggressive central bank tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: MoM change in CPIAUCSL > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months with MoM CPIAUCSL > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month MA for five consecutive months.
